summary.text: In a May 2026 speech, Jefferson said he was optimistic about AI's promise to drive productivity and growth while monitoring its effects on the labor market and inflation. He has also described AI as a real risk of labor disruption and said job loss is likely for certain firms and workers in certain occupations. In October 2026, he said AI-related spending was supporting business investment and expected AI-related investments to continue supporting growth. He has said it is likely still too soon to tell how AI's labor and price effects will affect monetary policy.

statements.text: AI has the potential to transform how we work and how we live, and it could have a profound effect on the economy.

attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: By automating certain tasks, it could lead to a reduction in some types of jobs. But increased productivity leads to economic growth, which may create new employment opportunities. AI is also expected to create new job categories and transform existing ones.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: On the other side of our dual mandate, price stability, AI could help the economy achieve higher growth through increased productivity while reducing inflationary pressures.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Conversely, AI could put upward pressure on certain price categories as many firms push to scale up the technology.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: So, what do these still-developing labor and price effects mean for monetary policy? The short answer is that it is likely still too soon to tell.

attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Some of the recent changes in hiring patterns, productivity growth, and inflation are likely to represent AI-driven change, but it is difficult to know the degree.

statements.text: AI can enable a worker to complete in seconds or a few minutes tasks that previously took many minutes, if not hours. Already, it is boosting worker productivity in a wide range of industries and occupations, including customer service, logistics, computer programming, and medical research.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: At the same time, many people have legitimate concerns that AI will cause job loss. At least for certain firms and workers in certain occupations, this is likely to be true.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: On the other side of our dual mandate—price stability—AI could help the economy achieve higher growth through increased productivity while reducing inflationary pressures. Specifically, increased productivity could lower production costs and put downward pressure on prices.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In terms of AI's implications for monetary policy, it is likely still too soon to tell. Policymakers must sort out changes in the economy that are due to cyclical factors from those resulting from structural change, which AI may well represent.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Productivity gains from AI may affect the relationship between employment and inflation and, hence, the conduct of monetary policy. Monetary policy decisions, of course, need to be made with a broad view of what is happening in the economy, not just in one sector or technology. There is still much to learn. I counsel exercising humility about the challenges in predicting AI's effects on employment and inflation.

attribution.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson

statements.text: A finding in the most recent survey is likely of particular interest to a conference exploring financial stability in a time of technological change—30 percent of contacts surveyed cited a turn in the prevailing sentiment toward AI as a salient risk to the U.S. financial system and the global economy. That was up from 9 percent in the spring survey. Participants noted that if such an unwinding were to occur, it could tighten financial conditions and restrain economic activity more broadly.
